answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): Individuals in the NLSY79 processed cohort with a criminal record (ever_jailed=1, jailed sometime in 1985–1994) had significantly lower wealth than those never jailed in ALL THREE measured years — 1985, 1990, and 1996 — with the gap widening sharply after the incarceration window (mean shortfall ≈ $17k in 1985, ≈ $58k in 1990, ≈ $85k in 1996; medians 720 vs 3,600, 0 vs 10,500, and 0 vs 8,500 respectively). However, because ever_jailed spans 1985–1994, the significant 1985 gap is pre-incarceration selection rather than an effect of incarceration; the significantly lower wealth in 1990 and 1996 persists even after adjusting for race, sex, and 1985 baseline wealth, consistent with — but not proof of — an incarceration-associated wealth penalty accumulating in the post-1985 years on top of pre-existing selection.

Detailed results (N=12,013; ever_jailed=1: n=289; ever_jailed=0: n=11,724; no missing values):

1) RAW per-year comparisons (jailed minus non-jailed):
- 1985: mean diff -17,157 (95% bootstrap CI -20,429 to -13,435); medians 720 vs 3,600. Welch t p=6.3e-21; Mann-Whitney p=1.6e-10; median test p=2.7e-09; Cliff's delta -0.22.
- 1990: mean diff -57,598 (CI -67,711 to -44,610); medians 0 vs 10,500. Welch p=1.6e-19; MWU p=7.8e-35; median test p=4.3e-35; Cliff's delta -0.42.
- 1996: mean diff -85,063 (CI -97,988 to -65,288); medians 0 vs 8,500. Welch p=7.3e-20; MWU p=9.3e-26; median test p=3.7e-18; Cliff's delta -0.35.
All raw p-values survive Holm correction across the three years (adjusted p < 1e-8 in every case), and every test agrees at any conventional alpha (0.05, 0.01, 0.001): the jailed group is significantly lower in wealth in 1985, 1990, AND 1996.

2) COVARIATE-ADJUSTED (HC1-robust OLS, ever_jailed + race + sex):
- 1985: beta -9,441 (SE 1,833), p=2.6e-07
- 1990: beta -35,394 (SE 6,309), p=2.0e-08
- 1996: beta -60,911 (SE 9,078), p=1.9e-11
All Holm-adjusted p < 1e-6. Race/sex adjustment shrinks but does not eliminate the gap; the coefficients grow over time.

3) BASELINE-ADJUSTED (1990/1996 additionally controlling 1985 wealth, isolating change from 1985 selection):
- 1990: beta -29,723 (SE 6,114), p=1.2e-06
- 1996: beta -55,905 (SE 8,964), p=4.5e-10
Holm-adjusted p < 1e-5. Even conditioning on pre-period wealth, jailed individuals lost/accumulated significantly less wealth by 1990 and 1996.

4) SENSITIVITY to skew (signed-log(wealth) regressions, race/sex adjusted): betas -1.09 (1985, p=4.5e-04), -3.38 (1990, p=2.3e-22), -3.53 (1996, p=4.6e-24) — same qualitative conclusion; the distributional tests (Mann-Whitney, median) and log-transform confirm the result is not driven by the extreme right tail (max values up to ~$4.06M vs 99th pct ≤ $1.4M) or by the ~30-38% zero/negative-wealth mass.

Timing caveat: since ever_jailed covers 1985–1994, the 1985 gap largely reflects pre-existing differences (selection); the 1990/1996 gaps reflect both that selection and any incarceration-period effect — the baseline-adjusted models suggest an incremental negative wealth change associated with jail status beyond 1985 levels, but causal attribution would require a stronger design (this dataset has no timing-of-jail detail). Composition note: jail prevalence is 5.3% (black), 3.2% (Hispanic), 1.0% (white), and 4.3% (male) vs 0.6% (female), which is exactly why race/sex adjustment was applied and why it modestly attenuated the raw gaps.

payload.hypothesis: Individuals with a criminal record (ever_jailed=1) had significantly lower wealth than those without in all three years measured (1985, 1990, 1996): mean wealth shortfall of ~$17k in 1985, ~$58k in 1990, and ~$85k in 1996 (medians 720 vs 3,600; 0 vs 10,500; 0 vs 8,500), significant in raw tests (Welch t, Mann-Whitney, median test; all Holm-adjusted p<1e-8), after adjusting for race and sex (HC1-robust OLS, p<=2.6e-07), and — for 1990 and 1996 — after additionally controlling 1985 baseline wealth (p<=1.2e-06). Because jail status spans 1985-1994, the significant 1985 gap indicates pre-incarceration selection, while the larger, baseline-adjusted gaps in 1990/1996 are consistent with an additional incarceration-associated wealth penalty.
payload.workflow: Inspected dataset (12,013 rows, no missingness; wealth composites right-skewed with zeros/negatives/extreme tails). Per year: Welch t-test, Mann-Whitney U, median test, bootstrap 95% CI of mean difference (5,000 resamples), Cliff's delta. Covariate-adjusted OLS with HC1 robust SEs (ever_jailed + race + sex); for 1990/1996 also controlled 1985 baseline wealth. Signed-log wealth sensitivity regressions. Holm correction across the three years for each test family. All conclusions robust across tests, adjustment sets, and correction.
